reviewedPrerequisites.reason: proc_filter uses NETLINK_CONNECTOR process events; PROC_EVENTS depends on CONNECTOR=y, so loading cn.ko alone cannot supply this test prerequisite.

run_test_fpu.sh checks modinfo/modprobe test_fpu; TEST_FPU depends on ARCH_HAS_KERNEL_FPU_SUPPORT and !KCOV_INSTRUMENT_ALL. The frozen collection has no config fragment; a built-in alone does not satisfy this original module-loading script.

configurationAudit.scope: Literal per-collection config and arm64 config.aarch64 fragments, reported separately without hiding conflicting requests. Pinned source-reviewed prerequisites are recorded separately; changed sources invalidate that review. Kconfig solving and other prerequisites need review. Differences are evidence, not test outcomes or inapplicability decisions.

runtimePolicy.upstreamTimeouts: collection settings retained except explicit source-declared or measured program overrides; outer watchdog adds 15 seconds cleanup and 60 seconds boot
runtimePolicy.modules: explicit per-kernel runtime payload; see module installation receipt

ublk:test_stress_05.sh.reason: Sequential recovery-mode phases launch fio --runtime=40 and wait for device removal; both kernels hit the inherited 45-second limit mid-workload. 600 seconds is an explicit measurement budget, not an upstream declared timeout.

rseq:run_param_test.sh.reason: The upstream collection declares timeout=0. The unchanged script runs 1184 invocations including injected yields, signals and sleeps; the 300-second unlimited-test fallback interrupted it. 7200 seconds is an explicit measurement budget, not a change to the test or its assertions.

cgroup:test_cpu.reason: The serial source workload requires at least 46 seconds: two 2-second CPU-time tests, four 10-second wall-time weight tests and two 1-second bandwidth tests. The collection default is only 45 seconds. 120 seconds is an explicit whole-program budget; all nine original assertions remain.

sched_ext:runner.reason: The 23-test serial suite includes CPU hotplug and two 1024-iteration scheduler attach/detach loops. The fixed TCG control completed its assertions just after the inherited 45-second deadline. 120 seconds is an explicit program budget, not an upstream timeout or changed test.

drivers/dma-buf:udmabuf.reason: The unchanged huge-page migration cases reserve and touch 1024 2 MiB pages. A 2 GiB VM cannot also hold the kernel and userspace. Use a separate 4 GiB machine on both Images without changing the 2 GiB allocation, assertions or timeout; the locked K6 machine is unchanged.

kvm:hello_el2.reason: The frozen kernel exposes KVM_CAP_ARM_EL2 only in its explicit nested mode on FEAT_NV2 hardware. The original test passes on Neoverse-N2 with kvm-arm.mode=nested; apply both prerequisites to both Images.

kvm:aarch32_id_regs.reason: The original test requires no AArch32 EL0 support, not merely an AArch64 kernel. Its RAZ/WI assertions pass on fixed A64FX; use that CPU on both Images without changing the test or timeout.

kvm:host_sve.reason: Cortex-A72 lacks the SVE capability required by the original test. The unchanged reference program passes on fixed Neoverse-N2; use that CPU on both Images without changing arguments or timeout.

kvm:demand_paging_test.reason: The original reference workload completes on fixed Neoverse-N2 within its unchanged 120-second limit; the Cortex-A72 control times out. Use the same CPU on both Images, preserving every guest mode and argument. This is a fixed-machine result, not a host-independent performance claim.

kvm:arch_timer.reason: The original 100-us timer margin fails with wall-clock TCG scheduling; all four reference vCPUs pass with instruction-clock execution. Keep arguments, assertions and timeout; this tests virtual timer semantics, not physical interrupt-delivery latency. Both Images use the same lane.

kvm.reason: The ordinary virt guest starts without EL2 and cannot expose /dev/kvm. Use the separate fixed-CPU EL2/GICv3 machine with 4 GiB on both sides (mmu_stress_test pre-faults 2 GiB before kernel/page-table overhead); keep the original Image, program arguments and timeout.

sched_ext:runner.reason: The unchanged hotplug test reaches cpu_die BUG on HVF; its fixed-CPU TCG control completes hotplug. Both compilers use the same declared lane.

drivers/dma-buf:udmabuf.reason: MEMFD_SIZE is 1024 and the huge-page cases set page_size to 2 MiB. Reserve the entire original 2 GiB HugeTLB request before the program on both Images; extra guest RAM alone does not populate this pool.

iommu:iommufd.reason: The unchanged domain_dirty128M_huge fixture maps 128 MiB with MAP_HUGETLB. Reserve 64 target 2 MiB hugepages before the original program on both Images; the ordinary one-page setup cannot satisfy this allocation.
